review:py.summary:
I reviewed the round-2 Python helper (remote.py, board.py, the two unit test files and remote_e2e.sh) against the saved old copy (fix7\python\before), capture_esp32c5.c, the patched capture_framework.c in /root/src/kismet, and Kismet cfe427074's kis_net_beast_httpd.cc and kis_datasource.cc. The three requested items are done and hold up.

**1. API key in a cookie.**
- A key goes out as 'Cookie: KISMET=<quote(key, safe="")>' and the URL has no query. This percent-encodes the same set of characters as the C patch's cf_ws_uri_escape.
- Kismet decodes the header with decode_uri and decode_cookies, and the last KISMET cookie wins. websocket-client puts cookies it stored from the server before ours, and it only stores cookies that name a Domain, which Kismet's do not.
- A login still goes as Basic, and a user name holding ':' still falls back to the query. A login wins over a key in both helpers.
- The warning for a user name with ':' and a login with '&' is the same text in both helpers.
- --connect localhost is unchanged: 127.0.0.1 first, with Host and Origin kept as 'localhost:<port>'.

**2. Refused channel set.** It matches refuse_channel and the framework's configure path: hopping is cancelled, an ERROR message is sent, then a success CONFIGREPORT with the reason and the unchanged channel. Kismet logs only messages, and reads a CONFIGREPORT's text only on failure. Channels are read the way sscanf("%u") reads them.

**3. Status texts.** Every board status, and the give-up text, now matches the C helper word for word, apart from the differences the implementer listed as intentional.

**Tests re-run on a snapshot of the files** (sha1s in py-review\base-sha1.txt; the repo was still identical at the end):
- Windows: test_board 238 PASS + 2 SKIP; test_kismet_v3 355 PASS + 2 SKIP. The extra SKIP is the TLS case, because there is no openssl on this shell's PATH.
- WSL venv: 254 and 358 PASS.
- tests/remote_e2e.sh from the snapshot on 2731/3731: 101 PASS, ALL OK, exit 0 (e2e-base.txt).
- The same new e2e with the old remote.py and board.py: 5 FAILs, all in the new checks (BTLE 40 answered with HTTP 500, and the proxy request line and cookie checks). So the e2e checks catch a revert. The run's kept /tmp log dir was removed, ports were free and nothing was left running.

**Mutation run** (26 mutants, mutations-1.txt): 23 were caught. Three survived: channel tracking in _tune (finding 2), the 'no PING … seconds' text, and passing the cookie in the header list instead of cookie=.

**add-to-kismet.sh** (sha1 58f0d13d…; the C agent was still editing it):
- On a fresh cfe427074 tree, then on a tree holding round 1's capture_framework.c, it produces identical capture_framework.c/.h.
- It copies unchanged helper files without touching them.
- A second run a few seconds later changes nothing, but a second run right after the first can touch the files autoconf generates (finding 5).

I did not check C/libwebsockets redirect handling, or any C code beyond reading it. Evidence is in scratchpad\fix7\py-review.

findings.title: The API key cookie now goes to any host a redirect points at (the old ?KISMET= URL did not)
findings.demonstration:
Script: py-review\redirect_demo.py; output in redirect_demo.txt and wsl_units.summary.txt. Server A on 127.0.0.1:2731 answers the upgrade with '302 Location: ws://127.0.0.2:3731/login', and server B on 127.0.0.2:3731 logs what it receives. The helper connects with remote.make_connector(apikey='SECRET-API-KEY').
- New code, websocket-client 1.9.2: B receives 'GET /login HTTP/1.1 ... Cookie: KISMET=SECRET-API-KEY'. The script prints '=== the API key reached the other host: True'. With 1.7.0 the result is the same.
- Old code (fix7\python\before): A received '...remotesource.ws?KISMET=SECRET-API-KEY', and B received no key ('... reached the other host: False').
- Cause: websocket-client follows up to 3 redirects and re-sends every option (header=, cookie=, host=, origin=) to the new Location, whatever its host or scheme. A redirect from wss to ws would therefore send the key in cleartext.
- Round 1's Basic Authorization header is forwarded the same way. This round extends the exposure to API keys.
- A reverse proxy that answers an unauthenticated upgrade with a 302 to a single-sign-on page (oauth2-proxy, Authelia) would receive the Kismet key or login.
findings.suggested_fix: Kismet never redirects remotesource.ws, so do not follow redirects. In WsTransport, pass redirect_limit=0 to websocket.create_connection. On 1.9.x a 3xx then raises 'Redirect limit exhausted'. On 1.7.0 and 1.8.0 there is no such guard, so also check ws.handshake_response.status after connecting and raise ConnectionError on any 3xx. Add a unit test that serves a 302 to another port and asserts that the second server never receives the Cookie or Authorization header. Check whether libwebsockets' client re-appends the handshake headers on a redirect for the C helper too.

findings.title: The hop-then-refuse test cannot detect a missing channel update: 6 is also the source's initial channel

Mutation: delete 'self.channel = str(number)' from Connection._tune (remote.py:1002).
- test_kismet_v3.py still ends ALL OK, exit 0 (mut-tune_no_channel_tracking-full.txt, line 227: "PASS hopped to 1 and 6 (6HT40), then refused 15: the answer is 6 ... {..., 2: '6'}").

- No other unit or e2e check catches this. The e2e refusal case is BTLE, where _tune returns early.

implement:c.summary:
I finished all seven C-side items. Every test passes: tests/c/run.sh, the full kismet_e2e.sh, and docker_smoke.sh on a freshly built image. Nothing was committed. Evidence is in the scratch folder `...\scratchpad\fix7\c\outputs` (proofs in `outputs\proofs\`, scripts in `scripts\`).

**1. Secrets out of the URL.** This is a framework patch in add-to-kismet.sh. It follows the same edit() style, is idempotent and has a skip note.
- **Login:** user and password now go in an `Authorization: Basic base64(user:password)` header. An API key goes in a `Cookie: KISMET=<key>` header, percent-encoded outside RFC 3986's unreserved characters, so '+' becomes %2B.
- **Where it lives:** the two values are new handler fields, `lwsauthorization` and `lwscookie`, in capture_framework.h. They are added in `LWS_CALLBACK_CLIENT_APPEND_HANDSHAKE_HEADER` with `lws_add_http_header_by_token`, and the base64 comes from `lws_b64_encode_string`. The URI is now just the endpoint.
- **Exception, same rule as the Python helper:** a user name containing ':' still goes in the query, percent-encoded. The helper warns only when such a user name comes with an '&' anywhere in the login; that function is now `warn_login_cannot_pass`, with the same wording as remote.py.
- **Unchanged:** user+password still wins over a key, with the existing 'Ignoring APIKEY' warning, and --tcp is untouched.
- **Long logins now fail with a message instead of being cut:**
  - The fallback URI is checked against its 1024-byte buffer.
  - The headers are checked against the room lws leaves. That is 3797 bytes here, so user:password can be about 2800 bytes.
  - On a header failure lws drops the connection without a connection-error callback. Without extra handling the process hung for good, which I saw in testing. The patch now sets shutdown and wakes the loop itself, so retry works.
- **Upgrading trees:** the script turns a round-1-patched tree into exactly the same files as a fresh cfe427074 tree (checked with cmp).
- **Wire proof, taken through a logging relay:**

review:c.summary:
I found one real regression and five small issues; everything else in round 2's C, framework-patch and Docker work checked out. I did not edit any repo file. Evidence is in C:\Users\oshria\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-oshria-OneDrive-Documents-GitHub-esp32c5-wireshark-sniffer\75fe8a4e-1aa2-48f3-9e8d-8f12a0275438\scratchpad\fix7\review-c\ (the scripts\ and outputs\ folders).

**The regression.** The framework now sends the login and the API key as request headers. libwebsockets (lws) adds those headers again on every redirect it follows, and it follows them, including to another host. So a server that answers the websocket request with a 302 gets the Basic login or the KISMET cookie passed on to wherever the redirect points. Round 1 did not do this: its login was in the query, which the redirect replaced. The Python helper refuses redirects for exactly this reason.

**What checked out:**
- **Base64:** the buffer is sized correctly for lws_b64_encode_string. Kismet's decoder handles the '=' padding.
- **Header room:** it is checked against lws's `len`, which is 3797 bytes here.
- **The ':' fallback and its warning** are the same as remote.py's `login_cannot_pass`, word for word.
- **Cookie:** the value is percent-encoded outside RFC 3986's unreserved characters, as Kismet's `decode_uri(...,true)` expects.
- **Precedence:** a login still wins over a key, with the "Ignoring APIKEY" warning.
- **Host and Origin:** the same as the round-1 binary (the wire capture in redirect.txt shows both).
- **No secret in the request line:** except the ':' fallback, which is by design.
- **smd_queue_depth guard:** the field and LWS_WITH_NETLINK are both in lws v4.2.0, 4.2.1 and 4.3.3. v4.1.6 has neither, so the guard is correct.
- **Older Kismet releases** (2021-06, 2022-01, 2023-07) read the cookie and Basic the same way.
- **add-to-kismet.sh:**
  - I ran it twice on a fresh cfe427074 tree under /tmp: the second run changed no file time.
  - The resulting capture_framework.c/.h, configure.ac, configure, Makefile.in and kismet_server.cc are byte-identical (cmp) to /root/src/kismet.
  - A tree holding the round-1 framework was upgraded to the same bytes, and a third run changed nothing.
  - kismet does not include capture_framework.h.
  - The /tmp trees are removed.
- **send_failed** stops both loops, and the helper no longer spins down itself.
- **tests/c/run.sh:** 321 PASS, ALL OK.

**The five minor issues:**
- A `--tcp` run with an unused ':' login of more than 1023 bytes is now refused.
- The e2e queue-warning check cannot fail on a machine with few routes.
- The "login does not fit" message tells you to use an API key even when the API key is what did not fit.

findings.title: The C helper sends the Basic login and the API-key cookie on to any redirect target, another host included; round 1 did not, and the Python helper refuses redirects
findings.demonstration:
scripts/redirect_demo.sh (outputs/redirect.txt). 127.0.0.1:2621 answers the websocket request with `302 Location: http://127.0.0.2:3621/elsewhere`, and 127.0.0.2:3621 logs every request head it receives. Run as `KISMET_CAP_USER=fx KISMET_CAP_PASSWORD='s3cret pw' kismet_cap_esp32c5 --connect 127.0.0.1:2621 --disable-retry --source esp32c5:device=...`.

New helper, what the other host receives:
```
== 127.0.0.2:3621 (the redirect's target, another host)
GET /elsewhere HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.2 ...
authorization: Basic Zng6czNjcmV0IHB3
```
That is fx:s3cret pw. With KISMET_CAP_APIKEY the other host receives `cookie: KISMET=DEADBEEF0123456789`.

Round-1 helper (/root/fix7c/before/kismet_cap_esp32c5): the other host receives `GET /elsewhere` with no login at all, because the query is dropped.

Python helper (outputs/redirect-python.txt): nothing reaches 127.0.0.2. It logs "the websocket was answered with a redirect (HTTP 302 to http://127.0.0.2:3621/elsewhere), which the helper does not follow ... the login would go along to wherever it points".

Cause: lws 4.3.3 client-http.c:698 follows 301/302/303/307/308 unless `client_no_follow_redirect` is set. It refuses only a TLS downgrade. `lws_client_reset` then calls LWS_CALLBACK_CLIENT_APPEND_HANDSHAKE_HEADER again, and HANDSHAKE_CASE adds the same headers. The framework sets only LCCSCF_USE_SSL (capture_framework.c ~2604).

When this matters: an SSO or auth proxy in front of Kismet (for example oauth2-proxy) sends unauthenticated requests to its identity provider with a 302. The C helper would then hand the Kismet admin login or the API key to that third party.
findings.suggested_fix:
In the framework patch, refuse redirects the way the Python helper does. Two ways:
- Set `caph->lwsci.ssl_connection |= LCCSCF_HTTP_NO_FOLLOW_REDIRECT;` next to LCCSCF_USE_SSL (the flag exists in lws 4.0 and later; guard it with LWS_LIBRARY_VERSION_NUMBER if older lws matters).
- Or add `case LWS_CALLBACK_CLIENT_HTTP_REDIRECT:` (lws 4.1 and later) to ws_remotecap_broker. It prints a FATAL naming the Location it did not follow and returns 1, so lws reports a connection error and the loop ends.

Mention it in the login fix's header note, and add an e2e check: a relay that answers 302 to a second listener, which must receive nothing.

findings.title: --tcp (which uses no login) is now refused when a ':' user name makes the websocket URI longer than 1023 bytes
findings.demonstration:
outputs/tcp-long-login.txt. Command: `kismet_cap_esp32c5 --connect 127.0.0.1:3621 --tcp --disable-retry --user a:b --password <1000 x> --source ...`.

New helper:
```
WARNING: Ignoring user, password, and apikeys in legacy TCP mode
FATAL: A user name with ':' puts the login in the websocket URI, which would be 1055 bytes long with it, more than the 1023 it can be; use an API key
```
Then the usage text, and exit 255.

Round-1 helper, same command: `INFO: Connected to '127.0.0.1:3621'...` and it goes on. That contradicts "--tcp is untouched".

Cause: the URI_HEADERS block runs whenever HAVE_LIBWEBSOCKETS is defined, whether or not `caph->use_tcp` is set, although only the websocket path uses lwsuri, lwsauthorization and lwscookie.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the login only for the websocket: `if (caph->use_ws) { ...URI_HEADERS... }`, or skip the length check when caph->use_tcp is set. Add a C harness case: --tcp with a ':' user and a long password must parse to 2.

findings.title: The e2e check for the lws queue warning passes with the fix reverted on any host with fewer than about 40 routes

outputs/smd-few-routes.txt. In a private network namespace (`unshare -n`, 5 IPv4 and 1 IPv6 routes), the round-1 helper, which lacks the fix, prints 0 'rejecting message on queue depth' lines. findings.title: The 'login does not fit' message says to use an API key even when the API key is what did not fit
